title: I Tracked the Bike-Cage Bluetooth Tag Through Three Tracker Apps

parts.text: Someone jammed a bluetooth tag under my saddle and walked the bike to the cage limit. The cage policy said: TAGS ON THE BOARD. NO SILENT PINGS. I was thirty, 4B, holding a missing-U-lock photo. App one showed a ping at 6:02 p.m. at the cage door. I posted the still in the building chat. The ping moved.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The ping just drifted toward the alley camera on app two.

social.video_title: A silent tag left the bike cage at 6:02 — Part 1/3
social.description: Missing U-lock, a cage ping, board policy. The ping moved toward the alley. Would you have followed it?

parts.text: App two was the alley cam the board had installed and forgotten. It caught a hoodie rolling my frame. I was still thirty, still 4B, now with two timestamps. I forwarded both to the super and to app three, the shop cam the bike store next door shared with us after the last walk. The hoodie went up the block with a saddle that had my scuff.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop cam has my scuff on a saddle in a hoodie hand.

social.video_title: The alley cam caught the hoodie rolling my frame — Part 2/3
social.description: Two timestamps, a shop cam, my scuff leaving. The super has the stills. Does the hoodie know about app three?

parts.text: The shop paused the hoodie at the stand. Police matched the three apps to a unit on 2. The bike came back. The tag became a building exhibit with a caption: SILENT PINGS ARE A POLICY. I get a U-lock that stays. 2G got a notice. The cage at 6:02 looks like a cage, which is to say steel and nobody's ping.

social.video_title: Three tracker apps found the ping — Part 3/3
social.description: Stand pause, a unit on 2, a tag exhibit. Was a saddle ever silent?
